newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Monday with investors uncertain about short-term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,890 yuan ($2,881) per tonne, rising 30 yuan.
It opened at 23,830 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,800 and a high of 23,990 yuan per tonne.
June fell 50 to 23,450, July 70 to 23,630, August 10 to 23,800, October rose 23,900 and November 90 to 23,840 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 46,440 tonnes from 72,480 tonnes.
Copper opened mixed and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said the market lost direction after prices met strong resistance last week at the 24,000-yuan level.
"There is no positive market-moving news around the corner to support any breach of that resistance level," a trader said. "Many investors would rather just wait and see what happens."
Physical copper in the Shanghai area is around 23,300 yuan per tonne, traders said.
In the absense of any local news, London Metal Exchange (LME) movements would be a major short-term factor, they said.
LME three months copper surged on Friday to near a one-year high of $2,488 per tonne, a jump of nearly $100 on the week, though it pulled back on profit-taking to close at $2,466.
Trading sources on Monday queried how much upside the red metal had, though many saw it ranging higher on the back of intermittent corrections.
"Shanghai copper will have difficulty rising above 24,000 yuan unless the LME rises sharply in the short term," a second trader said.

Aluminium ended mixed. June rose 10 yuan per tonne to 15,510, July fell 40 to 15,810, August unchanged at 15,850 and the September contracted, which traded for the first time, ended at 16,100 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 1,280 tonnes from 1,610 tonnes.
